Alex — thanks for the export and the clarity on timelines. Quick reply while we pull the full packet: I've attached a 1-page scorecard and a token-econ workbook that answers the three scenarios you asked for. Summary highlights below — full numbers in the PDF + spreadsheet.

Renewal scorecard (top-line)
- 90d total tokens: 1,860,000 tokens (65% gen/chat, 25% embeddings, 10% misc inference).
- 30d avg daily tokens: 21,400/day, ~2.1x increase YoY for same quarter.
- 95th p50 latency (production): 420ms -> up from 300ms 60d ago (peak periods).
- Error/timeout rate: steady at 0.4% (no spike).

Term options we recommend to present to Procurement
1) Standard renewal (12mo, existing list pricing) + 10% credit applied (fast contract turnaround).
2) Commitment uplift (12mo + 30% higher committed tokens): reduces effective per-token by ~22% vs current usage at run-rate; includes 10% burst buffer and 7-day overage grace. Best balance for cost efficiency.
3) Dedicated Pool (Reserved capacity): eliminates noisy tail latency during peaks, projected 40–55ms median latency improvement for your 95th percentile workloads; entails a 12–18mo commitment and a setup credit.

Performance notes: the dominant contributor to higher 95th latency appears to be increased embedding calls with long context lengths; we can reduce that impact with smarter batching and a light quantization profile for embedding models — we have a config we can apply in staging that won't change your model outputs materially.

Next steps
- I propose a 30-minute walk-through on Sep 1 (your local timezone) to run the scorecard and pick an option.
- If Procurement wants to see an ROI one-pager tailored to your internal SLA thresholds (p95 <= 350ms target), we can build that by Sep 2.

Attaching: Everwave_Redwood_Renewal_Scorecard_Aug29.pdf; token_economics_v1.xlsx
